en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Naked Ascetics, 45.
The Training Rule on Sitting Alone.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta went to a friend’s house and sat down alone with his wife in private.
Then that man complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can the noble Upananda sit down alone with my wife in private?"
The monks heard that man complaining, grumbling, and expressing his indignation.
Those monks who were few in desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and expressed their indignation, saying:
"How can the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan son sit alone with a woman in private?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, Upananda, that you sat alone with a woman in private?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... [as before]...
"How indeed, foolish man, could you sit alone with a woman in private?
This, foolish man, is not for the inspiration of those without confidence...
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whosoever, however, a bhikkhu should sit down in private with a woman, one-on-one, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whosoever, however, means whoever of such a kind... [etc. ...pe... [as above].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Woman" (mātugāma) means:

A human woman, not a female spirit (yakkhī), not a female ghost (petī), and not a female animal; one who is discerning and capable of understanding well-spoken and ill-spoken words, as well as what is grave and what is trivial.
"Together" means on one side.
"Alone with one" means there is both a monk and a woman.
"In private" means:
The seclusion of the eye, the seclusion of the ear.
"Seclusion of the eye" means that it is not possible to see [the object] while the eye is being pressed down, or while the eyebrows are being raised, or while the head is being lifted up.
"Privacy of the ear" means that it is not possible to hear ordinary conversation.
"Should sit down" means...
If a woman is sitting and a bhikkhu sits down near her or lies down near her, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If a bhikkhu is sitting and a woman sits down near him or lies down near him, there is an offense of expiation.
Or if both are sitting or both are lying down, there is an offense of expiation.
If, perceiving a woman as a woman, he sits down alone with her in private, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, being doubtful about whether she is a woman, he sits down alone with her in private, it is an offense of expiation.
If, perceiving one who is not a woman as a woman, he sits down alone with her in private, it is an offense of expiation.
If one sits alone with a female yakkha, a female peta, a paṇḍaka, or a human female who is an animal in form, in private, it is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If there is no woman present, but one perceives her as a woman, it is an offense of wrong-doing.
If there is no woman present, but one is in doubt, it is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if one perceives what is not a woman as not being a woman.
There is no offense if some other intelligent man is present as a companion.
He stands, he does not sit;
desiring the state of an Arhat,
he sits with his mind directed elsewhere.
"In the case of one who is insane,
and in the case of the first offender.
The fifth training rule concerning sitting in private is finished.
